country.evidence_quote: All subjects enrolled in this study included infants and adults from Ghana, Tanzania and Ethiopia

body_site.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from a Ghanaian cohort

family_role.evidence_quote: This cohort included 24 mothers and their infant(s) for a total of 50 metagenomes.

family_role.notes: Ghana/Tanzania described only as 'extended families' without explicit mother/father/child role assignment.

age_years.notes: Duplicate of `age` field, same aggregate mean values reported in years.

dna_extraction_kit.notes: Also used for Ghana/Tanzania/Ethiopia cohort DNA extraction as stated in Westernisation section.

extraction_warnings: The paper reports only aggregate demographic statistics (mean age, SD, range, % sex) per country/age-category subgroup for the Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania cohorts; no individual subject or sample identifiers are given in the extracted text, so subject_id and sample_id are not_reported and true sample-level rows could not be constructed.

Sex is reported only for adult subgroups (as aggregate percentages) in each country cohort; children/infant subgroup sex was not reported, and percentages could not be mapped to the single-value Female/Male enum without fabrication.

Supplementary tables (Table S1, S2, S4, S5) likely contain sample-level metadata (per-sample country, disease status, age, BMI, accession, etc.) that were referenced but not included in the provided text, limiting extraction to aggregate/subgroup-level statistics only.
Lifestyle, family, and family_role fields were inferred from narrative descriptions rather than a structured metadata table, and may not capture full within-cohort heterogeneity.

Case/control status for the CRC/T2D/IBD/hypertension/cirrhosis meta-analysis cohorts (Feng et al., Qin et al., etc.) was discussed at a high level but individual-level control/case assignments for those external datasets were not extracted since they are not the focus cohorts with detailed demographic data in this paper's own text.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['Ghana_adults', 'Ghana_children', 'Ethiopia_adults', 'Ethiopia_infants', 'Tanzania_adults', 'Tanzania_children']; kept batch 0.

This paper is a microbiome genomics/population-genetics study (Prevotella copri complex characterization) and does not report clinical treatment, tumor staging, biomarker, disease response, neonatal, or obstetric/gynecologic metadata relevant to most schema fields. Only 'disease_details' (Healthy status of newly sequenced cohorts) could be extracted with confidence.

The paper mentions disease-association meta-analyses across ten public datasets (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) but these refer to previously published external cohorts analyzed for clade prevalence/abundance, not primary participant-level clinical metadata collected in this study; therefore these were not extracted as disease_details to avoid conflating external dataset characteristics with this study's own subject metadata.

Isolate sourcing mentions 'healthy subjects and new onset rheumatoid arthritis patients' for P. copri strain isolation (Method Details), but this describes isolate donor status rather than the main cohort's clinical phenotype, so it was not included as a primary disease_details value; users should review if RA should be captured separately.

PMID not explicitly stated in text; paper_id (31607556) may represent it but this was not confirmed within the paper content.

target_condition field is ambiguous because the study's main focus is microbiome genomics rather than a single disease; listed diseases are those examined for association analyses using external cohorts.
Multiple sequencing platforms (HiSeq2500 and HiSeqX) were used across different sample types; only the most frequently mentioned (HiSeq2500) was selected for the enum field.
No curator or PMID metadata found in the main text; these were marked as not_reported.
